# Sirach Chapter 30 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 30 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**30:1** A father who loves his son will discipline him consistently — so that one day he'll be proud of him, not embarrassed in front of the neighbors.

**30:2** Discipline your son and he'll be worth something to you; you'll brag about him to your friends.

**30:3** Invest in your son's education and you'll make your enemies jealous; in front of your friends you'll beam with pride.

**30:4** When a father dies, it's as if he hasn't really died — because he left someone just like himself behind.

**30:5** He watched his son grow and rejoiced; when he died, he had no regrets.

**30:6** He left behind an avenger against his enemies and someone to repay kindness to his friends.

**30:7** Coddle your son and you'll be wrapping his wounds later; play favorites and every cry will shake you.

**30:8** A horse that's never been broken becomes unmanageable; a son who's never been corrected becomes willful.

**30:9** Spoil your child and he'll become your nightmare; play around with him all the time and he'll end up breaking your heart.

**30:10** Don't laugh everything off with him, or you'll end up crying; in the end you'll be grinding your teeth.

**30:11** Don't let him run wild when he's young; don't overlook his mistakes.

**30:12** Bend his neck while he's young; discipline him while you still can — otherwise he'll become obstinate, defy you, and your soul will ache.

**30:13** Work hard at raising your son, or his shameful behavior will trip you up.

**30:14** Better a poor man who is fit and strong than a rich man whose body is a constant torment.

**30:15** Good health, a sound body — these are worth more than all the gold there is; a robust constitution beats unlimited wealth.

**30:16** Nothing is a better treasure than a healthy body; no pleasure compares to a joyful heart.

**30:17** Death is better than a bitter life; endless sleep is better than never-ending illness.

**30:18** Pouring fine food into a closed mouth is like offerings laid before a tomb.

**30:19** What does an offering to an idol profit? It can't eat, it can't smell. The same is true of someone the LORD has brought low —

**30:20** they look on with their eyes and groan like a eunuch holding a young woman and sighing.

**30:21** Don't hand yourself over to grief; don't torture yourself with your own thoughts.

**30:22** A happy heart is life itself; joy of spirit is length of days.

**30:23** Cheer yourself up, comfort your heart; don't let sorrow take hold — it has killed many a person and there is nothing to show for it.

**30:24** Envy and anger cut years off your life; worry ages you before your time.

**30:25** A bright, cheerful heart will take pleasure in eating and look after what goes into it.
